care_team_notes: Use careful wording: a gene change can increase risk, but it does not guarantee MND. Encourage discussion with neurologist, MND clinic or genetic counselling service.
description: Australian MND-specific information on familial or inherited MND, common gene changes, family risk, sporadic MND and why genetic factors do not always mean a person will develop MND.
name: Familial MND and inherited risk

care_team_notes: Do not recommend a specific test. Suggest asking the treating neurologist what test is appropriate, how long results may take, what it may cost and whether counselling is available.
description: Explains diagnostic genetic testing for people already diagnosed with MND, including possible reasons to test, gene-targeted treatment/trial relevance and storage of DNA samples where appropriate.
name: Diagnostic genetic testing after MND diagnosis

care_team_notes: Flag that predictive testing is a personal decision with emotional and family implications. Recommend genetic counselling before testing.
description: Information for relatives asking whether MND runs in the family, including predictive testing, GP referral, genetic counselling and known family gene-change requirements.
name: Predictive genetic testing for family members

care_team_notes: For patient-facing answers, frame counselling as support for choice and understanding, not as pressure to test.
description: Explains what genetic counsellors do, how counselling supports decision-making, and why counselling matters for diagnostic and predictive MND genetic testing.
name: Genetic counselling before and after testing
publisher: MND Australia / Centre for Genetics Education

care_team_notes: Keep answers neutral and values-sensitive. Refer to genetic counsellor/fertility specialist for medical, ethical and cost details.
description: Australian MND-specific information on options for people planning a family where an MND-related gene change is known, including genetic counselling and pre-implantation/prenatal discussion pathways.
name: Family planning and reproductive options

care_team_notes: This is high-stakes financial/legal information. Encourage checking current guidance and speaking with a genetic counsellor or financial/legal adviser before applying for insurance or testing.
description: Current Australian information on genetic testing and life insurance, including the 8 October 2026 commencement of new protections and the interim moratorium context.
name: Genetic testing and life insurance in Australia
publisher: Centre for Genetics Education / Human Genetics Society of Australasia / Federal Register of Legislation

care_team_notes: Do not translate MSAC outcome into guaranteed patient eligibility. Use it as policy context and direct people to their neurologist/genetics service for individual access.
description: Australian MSAC application/outcome information for genetic testing in early-onset or familial neuromuscular disorders, useful for explaining Australian public funding/policy context.
name: Australian assessment of genetic testing for familial neuromuscular disorders

care_team_notes: When answering about tofersen/SOD1 or trials, cross-reference Topic 14 treatments and Topic 17 clinical trials. State when a source is US or UK.
description: Explains why genetic testing may matter for gene-targeted treatment or trial eligibility, while preserving that US therapy/regulatory information is non-Australian unless confirmed by Australian sources.
name: Gene-targeted treatment and clinical trial context

care_team_notes: Use after Australian sources. Always label as UK/US context and avoid applying non-Australian service, funding or insurance rules to Australian users.
description: UK/US explanatory material on inherited MND and genetic testing experiences, retained only as labelled non-Australian context where Australian sources do not provide enough detail.
name: Non-Australian inherited MND support material
publisher: MND Association UK / The ALS Association
